Profile evaluation report

See where you stand, and what to improve.

Answer 37 quick questions and 5 short written ones (about 11 minutes). Name the schools you want and they come first. You get your profile strength, how crowded your group of applicants is, and where you stand at each of 1,295 programmes, with the school’s own words and link. You also get a plan of what to fix first. Your “dream” schools depend on your own profile.

Why this one exists

Most feedback is a guess

Most profile feedback is one person’s view of your CV. This compares you with what 1,295 programmes publish, and shows the school’s own words and link for every result.

You compete with people like you

An Indian engineer with a 700 is not compared with the world average. They compete in one of the biggest groups of applicants. The report says this plainly.

It shows what will help

Each suggestion says how many more programmes it would open for you. If a change would not help, it says so.

Common questions

How long does it take?

About 6 minutes for the 37 main questions, and about 5 more for the 5 short written ones.

Will it tell me my chance of admission as a percentage?

No, and nothing here ever will. Anyone selling you a percentage is selling you a number with nothing behind it. This shows the gap between your profile and what a school published, which is a fact, and then it stops.

Why does it ask about gender and nationality?

Because they change the answer. Schools report their own class composition, and the size of the pool you are in affects the bar you face. Leaving those questions out would make the report more comfortable and less true.

Does anything I type get uploaded?

Not unless you press the button that asks for your email, and that button tells you exactly what it sends before you press it. The report itself is worked out in your browser.

When to talk to a person

This tool works from published facts. It cannot tell you which school to pick, how to explain a gap in your CV, or what your story is. Our consultants help with that.

Do I qualify for a waiver?

Check if you can skip the GMAT or GRE at 194 programmes.

194 programmes in our data say they can waive the GMAT or GRE. Each school sets its own rules. We check your profile against all of them, put each school in a group, and show the school’s exact words so you can check.

Why this one exists

194 programmes say the test can be waived

Each school writes its own rules, often in vague words. We read all of them for you.

120 have a rule we can check

The others say something like “the committee decides”. We show that clearly, so you do not plan around a maybe.

You see the school’s own words

For every programme we show the school’s own sentence, so you can check before you write to the school.

Common questions

Is a waiver the same as not requiring a test?

No. A waiver has conditions and someone decides. "Not required" means the test is not part of the application. This tool keeps them apart because the difference decides whether you book an exam.

What usually qualifies someone?

Most commonly: years of work experience, a quantitative degree, professional qualifications like the CFA or CA, or a prior graduate degree. Each school uses a different mix, which is why we check all 194.

Should I still take the test?

Often yes. A waiver removes a requirement; it does not add evidence. If your case rests on quantitative ability you have not otherwise shown, a score is still the cheapest way to show it. That is a judgement call, and it is one worth talking through.

Why this one exists

It asks what the question was first

An essay is an answer, and an answer can only be judged against what was asked. Paste the essay question too. The tool checks which of its key words never appear in your essay. Not answering the question is the most costly mistake, and no grammar checker will catch it.

Every finding shows you where

Not a list of counts you then hunt through. Your essay opens with each problem underlined in the text. Click a problem to jump to the exact words. Fix it there, and the counts update as you type.

It works whatever your first language is

146 rules across sixteen language backgrounds, split three ways: wrong anywhere, correct where you are from, and style. It never asks which one you are.

Common questions

Does it detect AI writing?

It counts ten signals that make a draft look machine-written and gives you a band, not a verdict. No detector is reliable enough to accuse anyone, and this one does not.

Is my essay uploaded?

The grammar, cliche and score passes run in your browser, and so does the editor — typing in it sends nothing anywhere. Your essay is never sent anywhere. The email form sends only its word count.

Why does it ask for my email?

The score, the length and the does-it-answer-the-question check are open to anyone. The working view — your draft marked up, every finding pointing into it, the editor — opens once you give a name and an address. It costs nothing, and it is asked once.

Will it write my essay?

No. An essay written by a machine reads like one, which is the problem this tool exists to find.

When your money has to be there

Not how much. The date.

For a student visa you must show money in the bank. Some countries also say how long it must stay there. This tool tells you the last day to put the money in. Miss that day and your visa can be refused, even if you have enough money.

Why this one exists

The amount is the easy part

It is printed on a government page. Every consultancy quotes it.

The date is what catches people

Most countries require the money to have been sitting in the account for a set period. Move it a day late and the amount is irrelevant.

Every figure from a government page

Five countries, each with the source and the date it was checked, because a stale financial requirement is the most expensive mistake on this site.

Common questions

What is "seasoning"?

The period the funds must already have been in the account before you apply. The UK is 28 consecutive days. Others differ, and some do not publish one — those are shown blank rather than guessed.

Can I use my parents’ account?

Sometimes, with specific evidence of the relationship and their consent. The rules differ by country and are one of the more common refusal reasons, so read the source link before assuming.

Why are some countries missing a date?

Because the authority does not publish one. We show the blank rather than invent a figure somebody would book a flight around.

True cost and payback

Fees are only part of the cost.

This tool adds up fees, living costs, loan interest and the savings you miss while studying. Then it shows, in rupees, the month the degree pays for itself.

Why this one exists

Tuition is not the number

The number that decides whether the degree paid off is tuition plus living plus loan interest plus the salary you did not earn while studying.

In rupees, with your own figures

Your salary, your loan, your rate. Not a worked example from a brochure.

It names the month you break even

Not a range, not a feeling — the month, given what you typed.

Common questions

Does it include the opportunity cost?

Yes, and that is usually the largest single line. Two years out of a growing salary costs more than most people count.

What exchange rate does it use?

The one you type. Rates move, and a tool that fetches a live rate and then sits in your browser for a week would be quietly wrong.

Is a longer payback a bad sign?

Not on its own. A ten-month masters in Europe and a two-year American MBA are different products with different ceilings. The payback month is one input to that decision, not the decision.

Visa and post-study work rights

Answered for your passport.

How long each country lets you stay and work after you graduate, and what comes next. The answer depends on your passport, so we ask for it. For example, an Indian passport gives you an extra year in Australia and in France. Every fact has a date and a link to the government page.

Why this one exists

It answers for your passport

An EU passport removes the permit entirely in eight of these countries. An Indian one is worth an extra year in Australia and a second year in France. A generic answer is wrong for almost everyone.

And for your course and your college

France will not issue below master grade. The United States gives 12 months or 36 depending on a six-digit code. The UK has a route that requires your degree to be from a named list and NOT to be British. One number per country cannot express any of that.

26 routes, every one from a government page

Read on 7 September 2026, each with the link. Immigration rules change on political timelines, so the date matters as much as the number.

Common questions

Is this a work visa or a job-search visa?

It depends on the country, and they are not the same thing. Spain’s says plainly that you may not work on it. The UK’s Graduate visa lets you work outright. The tool labels each one, because the difference decides what you do in month one.

My programme is an MBA — is that STEM in the US?

Usually not. Eligibility runs on the six-digit CIP code your programme is registered under, and a standard MBA is 52.0201, which is not on the list. A growing number of business masters are registered under codes that are. Ask the school for its CIP code.

Why does it sometimes say I have no route?

Because on the answers you gave, none of the published routes is open. That is usually one condition, and it is usually fixable. The full report names which one, for each route.

How current is this?

Every route carries the date it was read and a link to the page. Check again before you apply. An old visa rule is the most dangerous mistake on this site, because it can change which country you choose.

Should I sign anything before I arrive?

Because sourcing them properly is about twelve days of work and it has not been done yet. That is a real gap and the page says so rather than filling it with generic advice.

Common questions

Can I reuse my university statement of purpose?

No. The university asks why you deserve a place. The visa officer asks whether you are a genuine student who will comply with the conditions. They are different documents with different answers.

How early should I start?

As soon as you have an offer. Appointment backlogs, not paperwork, are what make people miss an intake.

Is this immigration advice?

No. It is a summary of published requirements. Only the authority named on each source can tell you what applies to your case.

Why this one exists

A short, honest list

Many intakes close early. The honest answer to “what can I still apply to?” is often a short list.

Counted from published deadlines

Not from a sense of what is usually open. From dates schools actually printed.

And the far larger number we cannot answer for

Most programmes do not publish a date we can read. That count is shown next to the list, at the same size, because hiding it would make the list look bigger than it is.

Common questions

Why can you not read most deadlines?

Because they are written as prose, or as rounds with no year, or not published at all. We are working on reading more of them. Until then, we show how many we could not read.

Does "still open" mean I should apply?

It means the door is open. Applying three days before a deadline with an essay written in two of them is usually worse than waiting for the next intake.

How often does this update?

The comparison runs against today’s date every time you open it. We update the deadlines when we re-check the schools’ websites. Each one shows the date we read it.

interview-practice-room.title: Interview practice room
interview-practice-room.html:
Home›Free tools›Practice and deadlines
Practice and deadlines

Interview practice room

Practise with a real clock, like the real thing.

Practise for two kinds of interview. In a recorded interview (like Kira Talent), a question appears, a timer runs and you record one answer. Nobody is there. In a live interview, a real person asks you questions and follow-ups. This room does both, with 141 questions based on what schools say they ask, including questions about your own CV. After you answer, it shows what you said, how you said it, and what you left out.

  • Recorded and live interviews
  • 141 questions, in groups
  • Questions for your school
  • Your looks are never scored
Talk to a consultant

Open Interview practice room in a new tab

Why this one exists

A Kira has no interviewer. A real one does.

They are different skills and most practice tools blur them. In a recorded assessment nobody is there — no follow-up, no chance to ask what they meant, one take. In a live interview a person who has read your file can push back. The room keeps the two apart and asks what each one asks.

Every series a school can ask, and you pick the school

Choose your school, and its name appears in every question about it. For example: which specialisation you would take there. Then pick a group of questions: opening, why this school, goals, your CV, behavioural, values, what you contribute, opinion and ethics, situations, self-awareness, curveballs, the written question, follow-ups, and questions you ask them. The questions come from what GMAC, EDHEC, INSEAD, HBS, MIT Sloan, Wharton and HEC Paris say they ask. We do not guess this year’s questions.

It measures. It does not judge your face.

How fast you spoke, your filler words, how your answer was built, and points from your CV that you did not use. There is no score for confidence or enthusiasm. EU law (the AI Act) does not allow guessing emotions in education, and it cannot be done honestly anyway.

Common questions

Are these the real questions my school will ask?

No, and be wary of anyone who says theirs are. Schools randomise, rewrite between rounds and keep the bank confidential. These are the kinds of questions schools and test makers say they ask. They are written out in full so you can practise. Where a question comes from a published list, we name the source.

Where do the recordings go?

Nowhere. They are recorded, measured and played back in your browser. One button sends a single recording to an Involve consultant for review. It tells you this before you press it.

Does it work in French, Spanish or German?

Yes. Each language has its own list of filler words and unsure words, and its own normal speaking speed. We do not just translate the English rules. The page also tells you whether a native speaker has signed off each list yet.

What does it cost?

Nothing. The room, the recording, the self-review and the measured report are all free. Your first 2 reports are free. After that we ask for your name and email once. That is all it costs. We ask so we can follow up if your answer shows something worth talking about.

How many times should I practise?

Enough that the format stops being the hard part. Not so many that the answer becomes recited — a memorised answer is audible, and it is worse than a rougher honest one.
